key_assumptions.input: Starting free cash flow per share
key_assumptions.source: FY2025 free cash flow: cash from operations $2,010M minus capital spending $371M = $1,639M, divided by 281M diluted weighted-average shares (10-K filed 2026-02-20, fiscal year ended 2025-12-31)
Mid-single-digit system sales growth converts to mid-single-digit owner cash via unit development (63K+ units) and +3% same-store sales; Taco Bell U.S. strength offsets Pizza Hut; debt service stable

open_questions: Debt-funded buybacks: sustainable at **$11.9B** long-term debt versus **$1.64B** FY2025 FCF?
Habit Burger strategic options (re-franchise vs exit).
Pizza Hut franchisee closure rate monitoring.
thesis: Yum! Brands, Inc. (YUM) is one of the world's largest quick-service restaurant franchisors, operating four global concepts: **KFC**, **Taco Bell**, **Pizza Hut**, and **Habit Burger & Grill**. **[Fact]** As of December 31, 2025, the system comprised **63,285** restaurants in **155** countries and territories; **97%** of units are franchised. **[Fact]** FY2025 **system sales** were **$68.3 billion** (+4% reported); **reported revenues** (franchise fees, royalties, company-store sales, and advertising contributions) were **$8.21 billion** (+8.8% versus $7.55 billion in FY2024). **[Fact]** FY2025 cash from operations was **$2.01 billion**; capital spending was **$371 million**; free cash flow was approximately **$1.64 billion**, or about **$5.83** per diluted share on **281 million** shares. The company collects royalties and franchise fees on franchisee sales rather than operating most stores directly.
why_market_wrong: There is **no dated mispricing catalyst** (HK predictive attribute: **none**). **[Inference]** Generalists may anchor on GAAP net income (**$1.56 billion**, flat versus $1.49 billion prior year) and elevated leverage (**$11.9 billion** long-term debt) while underweighting the asset-light franchise cash engine: **$68.3 billion** of system sales converting to **$2.01 billion** of operating cash flow with limited capital intensity. **[Fact]** Same-store sales turned positive at **+3%** in FY2025 after **-1%** in FY2024; Taco Bell U.S. momentum and international KFC unit growth are the mix drivers (10-K FY2025). **[Fact]** Q1 2026 revenues rose **15%** year over year to **$2.06 billion** with diluted EPS **$1.55** versus **$0.90** prior year, but lapping and tax timing affect quarterly comparability. **[Inference]** The inefficiency is **descriptive** (quality franchise compounder at a full price with leverage), not a timed equity yield-curve setup.
